verdict.summary: The exact reconciliation head introduces a trust-boundary regression in required-check evaluation: protection-required checks outside the release policy are silently omitted across all callers, not only main-branch evidence.

blockingFindings.title: Protection-required checks are dropped from PR and release-evidence verification
blockingFindings.details: At head 14e5de0d0982068e89a5039023734f713fc54e8a, evaluateRequiredChecks now ignores every branch-protection binding not already present in policyChecks. This shared function is also used by ensureReleasePull, both reconciliation paths, and verifyReleasePullEvidence with real branch protection. Consequently, an additional required protection check can be missing or red while DarkFactory reports its reduced check set green, arms automerge, and later claims the trusted PR gates were green. GitHub may still delay the merge, but DarkFactory's recorded evidence and decisions no longer represent the complete required gate set. Scope the policy-only behavior to main verification/observation (for example through the existing includeProtection:false mechanism) while retaining the union of policy checks and protection-required checks for protected-PR and historical gate verification.

nonBlockingNotes: The added test covers policy-selected main evidence but does not cover the shared function's protected-PR callers with an additional required protection check.
